ConocoPhillips rose slightly today as oil markets steadied following a sharp drop two days earlier. The stock has bounced back from a low of $132.19 on November 23rd—the day climate talks at COP31 collapsed without committing to phase out fossil fuels. That collapse, which had initially spooked energy investors, actually removed a source of near-term regulatory uncertainty for oil companies, allowing the stock to recover toward its prior levels.

The modest gain also reflects a stabilizing geopolitical backdrop. While tensions persist around Russian refinery attacks and retaliatory threats, the broader global energy picture has steadied: U.S. crude is trading at $82.24 per barrel and international crude at $91.80, within normal ranges for the past few weeks. The failed climate deal removes the risk of a binding international commitment that could have constrained future oil demand, which keeps the investment case for major oil producers intact for now.
